messages:
Maya (devex): Installing the Python SDK in a Windows venv fails with an SSL cert verify error. Repro on 3.8/3.11/3.12.
Maya (devex): Command: `python -m venv .venv && .\.venv\Scripts\activate && pip install redwood-inference`
Maya (devex): Error: `ssl.SSLCertVerificationError: [SSL: CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED] certificate verify failed (_ssl.c:1123)`
Sam (sdk): thanks. are you behind a proxy or using corp CAs? can you run `python -c "import ssl, certifi; print(ssl.get_default_verify_paths(), certifi.where())"`?
Liam (windows): Windows Python builds sometimes don't populate openssl cafile paths, and pip may build from sdist which relies on system OpenSSL that doesn't see Windows cert store.
Maya (devex): Output: `DefaultVerifyPaths(cafile=None, capath=None, openssl_cafile_env=None, openssl_cafile=None, openssl_capath_env=None, openssl_capath=None)`
Maya (devex): `certifi.where()` -> `C:\\\\Users\\\\maya\\\\AppData\\\\Local\\\\Programs\\\\Python\\\\Python311\\\\Lib\\\\site-packages\\\\certifi\\\\cacert.pem`
Sam (sdk): quick workaround: `pip install certifi` then set `SSL_CERT_FILE` to the certifi path (Windows cmd: `set SSL_CERT_FILE=...`; Powershell: `$env:SSL_CERT_FILE=...`). That should let pip verify TLS during install.
Maya (devex): workaround worked. but this is bad for first-time users. we should fix packaging and docs.
Sam (sdk): proposed fixes: 1) publish prebuilt wheels for cp38-cp312-win_amd64 so pip won't fall back to sdist; 2) support `REDWOOD_CA_BUNDLE` env var and fall back to certifi if no system cafile; 3) add a Windows quickstart troubleshooting note.
Liam (windows): when we build wheels, we should document MSVC toolchain and OpenSSL version, and ensure wheels are linked consistently to avoid runtime cert/openssl ABI issues.
Jess (qa): add Windows smoke install in the CI matrix for 3.8-3.12 `pip install . && python -c "import redwood_inference; print('ok')"`. That would catch regressions early.
Maya (devex): also noticed typing gaps: `AsyncClient` methods lack proper typed overloads, so mypy/autocomplete shows Any. this hurts DX.
Sam (sdk): agreed. let's ship PEP 561-compatible type stubs with the wheel release (or include and annotate inline). I'll open a meta-issue that tracks wheels, cert bundle env var, and stubs.
build-bot: created issue https://github.com/redwood-inference/python-sdk/issues/433 (windows wheels + ca fallback + typing stubs) :white_check_mark:
Liam (windows): note for issue: include target OpenSSL ABI and MSVC runtime. also validate that the wheel's metadata declares `Platform: Windows` correctly.
Jess (qa): assigning QA to add the Windows matrix and smoke job.
Sam (sdk): I'll coordinate packaging and docs updates. thanks for the clear repro, Maya.
Maya (devex): will draft a quick Windows troubleshooting blurb for the quickstart and open a docs PR. :memo:
